summary: A 1949 L-4 tower from Sawyer Ridge, retired by the Forest Service in 1987 and faithfully rebuilt as the private "Eyeful Tower" beside the Drehers' home.

facts.design: L-4 cab, 14x14 ft, on a 41 ft treated timber tower
facts.status_note: Private residence property; restored, tours by pre-arrangement only.

access.note: On the Drehers' private property; tours available only by pre-arrangement, per NHLR.

facts.agency: Bruce and Nancy Dreher (private owners); originally Nez Perce National Forest

events.note: Erected on Sawyer Ridge, Nez Perce National Forest, as a 41 ft timber tower with L-4 cab.
David Emmons staffed the tower in 1972 and transferred out at season's end; the only named staffer found.
Declared surplus to Forest Service needs and sold.
Purchased by Bruce and Nancy Dreher and moved to their private property overlooking the Slate Creek Ranger Station.

Rebuilt and renamed the "Eyeful Tower"; NHLR describes it as a careful, accurate rebuild. No source states the Drehers' motive for buying it (the original note that it was bought to save it from demolition was unsupported and removed).
Registered February 24, 1996, as NHLR US 163 / ID 13, nominated by Idaho registrar Gary Weber.

notes_for_editor: NHLR gives elevation 7,273 ft at the Dreher property; idahofirelookouts.com gives 7,303 ft for the original Sawyer Ridge site — left unreconciled since they describe two slightly different points and neither source is clearly authoritative for the other's site. No source gives who built the original tower (a crew, not a named builder) or the exact reason the Forest Service decided it was surplus beyond space/staffing needs implied by the 1987 date. No current rental status or public visiting hours beyond 'by pre-arrangement' were found.
